What to Expect from a Dedicated Iowa OWI Under 21 Defense Attorney

Iowa law treats drivers under 21 differently regarding OWI. The legal limit for adults is a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08%. For drivers under 21, Iowa enforces a much stricter standard — a BAC of just 0.02% or higher can trigger an OWI charge.

That small number can lead to serious consequences, including license suspension, fines, and a criminal record. At Henkels & Baker, PC, based in Dubuque, Iowa, we help young drivers and their families understand what an OWI charge means and what legal options may be available.

An OWI under 21 is not a minor issue. It can affect school, employment, and driving privileges for years. The sooner you speak with an OWI under 21 defense attorney in Iowa, the more options you may have.

Iowa courts handle underage OWI cases through a process that involves both criminal charges and administrative license actions. These are two separate tracks, and both matter. However, a charge does not mean a conviction is certain.

There may be ways to challenge the stop, the testing method, or the evidence.

Our goal at Henkels & Baker is to review every detail of your case and work toward the most favorable outcome.

How Henkels & Baker Fights Iowa Under-21 OWI Charges

At Henkels & Baker, PC, our first step is to look closely at the facts of your case. We review the traffic stop, the field sobriety tests, and any breath or chemical test results. Every detail matters.

Zero-tolerance laws in Iowa are strict.

For drivers under 21, a blood alcohol content (BAC) of just .02 or higher can lead to an OWI charge. That means even a small amount of alcohol may trigger serious legal consequences.

We look at how the stop was made. Law enforcement are required to have a valid reason to pull you over. If that reason is weak or unclear, we may be able to challenge the stop itself.

We also review how any testing was done.

Breathalyzer devices have to be properly maintained and used correctly. If the device was faulty or the test was administered incorrectly, those results may not hold up. Our team looks for those issues right away.

When your driver’s license is at risk, timing is critical. Iowa has a short window to request a hearing before your license is suspended. We work fast to protect your driving privileges while your case moves forward.

Not every case goes to trial. We look at all paths — including reducing charges or pursuing a plea that keeps the worst outcomes off the table.

Our goal is to protect your record, your license, and your future. One charge should not define the rest of your life. We take that seriously at every step.

Why Choose Henkels & Baker to Handle Your Under-21 OWI Case

Here’s what we can offer:

What Happens After an OWI Under 21 Charge in Iowa

Iowa handles OWI under 21 cases through a clear set of steps. Each stage has its own timeline and its own demands.

Here is what you can expect from arrest through resolution.

Stage 1: Arrest and Initial Charges (Day 1–7)

After an arrest, Iowa law requires a court appearance within a short window — often within 24 to 48 hours for an initial hearing. You will be formally advised of the charges. At this stage, your job is to say nothing beyond what is legally required.

Your attorney begins right away — reviewing the arrest report, the officer’s notes, and any chemical test results.

Stage 2: Administrative License Revocation (First 10 Days)

Iowa’s implied consent law triggers automatic license revocation for drivers under 21 who test at or above 0.02 BAC or refuse testing (Iowa Code § 321J.6). You have only 10 days from the date of arrest to request a hearing with the Iowa Department of Transportation to contest the revocation. Missing this window means your license is suspended automatically.

Your attorney files the hearing request and builds the challenge to protect your driving privileges while the criminal case moves forward.

Stage 3: Arraignment and Plea (Weeks 2–4)

Your arraignment takes place in your county’s Iowa District Court. You enter a formal plea — typically not guilty at this stage. Your attorney handles court appearances so you do not have to face them alone.

A not guilty plea keeps all options open and gives your attorney time to review the full evidence file.

Stage 4: Pre-Trial Review and Negotiation (Weeks 4–12)

This is the most active part of the process. Your attorney requests all discovery — police body cam footage, field sobriety test records, and calibration logs for any breathalyzer used. Under Iowa law, improper testing procedures or unlawful stops can be grounds to suppress evidence.

Your attorney may also negotiate with the prosecutor during this window. For first-time offenders, Iowa courts sometimes allow alternatives such as a deferred judgment, which may keep a conviction off your record.

Stage 5: Trial or Resolution (Month 3 and Beyond)

Most cases resolve before trial through a plea agreement or a dismissal. If the case goes to trial, it proceeds in the Iowa District Court for your county — Dubuque County District Court if the arrest happened locally. Your attorney presents the defense, cross-examines witnesses, and challenges the state’s evidence.

Timelines vary, but most OWI cases involving individuals under 21 in Iowa resolve within three to six months from the date of arrest.

Throughout every stage, your attorney keeps you informed. You will know what is due, what is happening, and what your options are at each step.

As an OWI under 21 defense attorney in Iowa, our firm knows how much is at stake. We review the facts of your case and work toward a favorable outcome. You deserve clear answers — not confusion.

Reach out now and schedule an initial consultation. Do not wait for the court date to get help. Contact Henkels & Baker, PC today.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Can I be charged with OWI under 21 even if I wasn’t driving?

Iowa law may apply operating while intoxicated charges if you were in physical control of a vehicle, not just actively driving it. Sitting in the driver’s seat with the keys nearby can be enough in some cases.

2. Will an OWI charge show up on my college application background check?

A charge — not just a conviction — may appear on certain background checks, depending on how the check is run. Resolving the case early or seeking a dismissal may help limit what shows up.

3. What if I refused the breath test during my traffic stop?

Iowa’s implied consent law means refusing a test can trigger an automatic license revocation, separate from any OWI charge. Your attorney can review whether the stop and test request were handled correctly under Iowa law.

4. Does an OWI under 21 affect my ability to get a job in Iowa?

Many Iowa employers run criminal background checks, and an OWI conviction may raise concerns depending on the role. Pursuing a strong defense now can reduce the risk of a permanent record that would affect future job opportunities.

5. How long does the Iowa OWI process typically take for someone under 21?

Most Iowa OWI cases resolve within a few months, though complex cases may take longer depending on the county court’s schedule. Your attorney can give you a clearer timeline once the details of your case are reviewed.
